segment.description: Middle Fork Obion River, a principal fork of the Obion system (HUC 08010203), flowing from its upper reach near Como (Henry/Carroll county line area) through Weakley County (Gleason, Sharon, Dresden) into Gibson County (Sidonia) toward the fork confluences; catalog describes it as a principal Obion fork whose access and lowland conditions vary by reach.
segment.boundaries: Catalog gives no explicit boundaries; documented evidence reaches are the USGS-gaged upper reach near Gleason (07024705) and near Sidonia (07024790), plus TDEC stations MFOBI026.3HN (upper, near Como), MFOBI014.6WY and MFOBI004.5WY (lower, Weakley County).

coldSource.notes: Gage elevation 360.00 ft NGVD29 at 07024705 near Gleason, falling to about 310 ft at the downstream Sidonia gage (USGS site service) — a low-gradient West Tennessee bottomland fork in the channelized Obion system (TWRA 2015 SWAP Obion River COA).

holdover.detail: No holdover trout fishery documented. TWRA stocks no trout on the Middle Fork Obion River (the county-level winter rainbow sites are ponds/parks such as McKenzie City Park and Milan City Pond), and the TN Trout Management Plan states hatchery-supported warmwater habitats 'cannot support trout year round.'

wildPopulation.detail: Dickinson's 1973 UT survey of the Obion River system — most collections from the Reelfoot Lake area and the principal forks of the system — verified 100 fish species and lists no salmonids.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: A USGS grab at the Sidonia gage measured 29.0 C in August 1988, and TWRA stocks no trout on this channelized warmwater fork.
